input.question: Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in C[z] whose Hessian matrix Hes P is nilpotent, so P is Hessian nilpotent. If Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 is the Laplace operator on C[z], must the iterated Laplacians of the powers of P eventually vanish in the sense that Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?

original_paper.title: Hessian nilpotent polynomials and the Jacobian conjecture

rewritten_question: Let P(z_1, ..., z_n) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 with complex coefficients. Write Hes(P) for its Hessian matrix, whose (i,j)-entry is the second partial derivative ∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j. Suppose this Hessian matrix is nilpotent, meaning that some power of Hes(P) is the zero matrix. Let Δ = ∑_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2 be the Laplace operator on the polynomial ring C[z_1, ..., z_n]. Is it true that for all sufficiently large integers m one has Δ^m(P^{m+1}) = 0?

paper_evidence.quote: Let P(z) ∈ C[z] and Hes(P) denote the Hessian matrix of P. We call P Hessian nilpotent if Hes(P) is nilpotent.
Let Δ := ∑_{i=1}^n D_i^2 be the Laplace operator on C[z].
Problem 1.1. Let P(z) be a Hessian nilpotent polynomial. Is it true that Δ^mP^{m+1} = 0 when m \gg 0?
